name: caffeinity-skills
description: Caffeinity skills marketplace: editing, teaching, recruiting, SEO, release-preflight, decision review, and multi-agent tournament plugins.

plugins.name: wordsmith
plugins.description: Teaches your agent to edit, not just generate: 44 commands across 5 disciplines that tighten, rewrite, critique and proofread while keeping the author's meaning, hedges and voice intact.

plugins.name: recruiter-lens
plugins.description: Reviews resumes, CVs and LinkedIn profiles the way recruiters screen them: first-impression scans, ATS compatibility, rejection-pattern diagnosis and interview prep. Never invents a metric.

plugins.name: topic-primer
plugins.description: A world-class teacher for any topic, from zero background toward expert depth, in eight modes from foundations and curricula to strict exams and ELI5.

plugins.name: do-better
plugins.description: When an answer is bad, runs a single-elimination tournament of sub-agents with different strategy cards until one solution survives.

plugins.name: keyword-guard
plugins.description: Plans topic clusters and kills keyword cannibalization so exactly one page wins each query, with a mandatory cannibalization audit before content changes.

plugins.name: web-preflight
plugins.description: Checks a site you own before you ship it, treating status codes as signals rather than findings; unrun checks are reported as INCONCLUSIVE, never a pass.

plugins.name: applicant-kit
plugins.description: Produces tailored job-application material: decoded JD table, action-task-result-impact bullet rewrites, honest keyword placement map, five role-specific summaries, full LinkedIn rewrite, and a 20-question interview answer pack. Sibling of recruiter-lens: it produces while recruiter-lens judges. Never invents experience or numbers.

plugins.name: findable
plugins.description: Sets up discovery for a GitHub repo, agent skill, Claude Code plugin or MCP server so people and agents find it by what it does, not just its name: audits current visibility and same-name collisions, derives the queries strangers actually type, drafts the About text, topics, README opening, release notes and a project page, then plans directories and a dated re-check. Never games stars or leaves example slots with invented output.

plugins.name: application-pilot
plugins.description: Runs the job search around the applications: search brief, role discovery with honest posting dates, rubric-based fit scoring, a reviewable CSV or Markdown tracker, follow-up drafts, interview briefings and a funnel review. Never submits, invents nothing, and has no CLI, telemetry, or browser automation. Coordinates with applicant-kit and recruiter-lens.

plugins.name: crash-test
plugins.description: Crash-tests a decision before you build it. Four fixed roles (Pragmatist, Skeptic, Specialist, Contrarian) draft the same task in separate contexts, attack each other's drafts anonymously, and a chair merges what survived, keeps a dissent log, and grounds the winner's claims against your source before adopting it. Optional Operator seat for cost, rollout and reversibility. No server, no API keys, no other agent CLIs.

plugins.name: pre-ship-performance-audit
plugins.description: Audits and fixes web app performance before launch: four read-only subagent audits over twenty known slow-downs across images, fonts, bundles, database queries and servers, then same-condition mobile Lighthouse medians prove each fix. Never removes a feature for a score; asks before dependency, index, RLS or region changes.

plugins.name: pre-ship-security-red-team
plugins.description: Authorized, evidence-driven red-team pass over a web app you own, before launch. Three read-only subagents run 14 authorization and abuse checks against isolated synthetic accounts, the chair fixes each failure, adds regression tests, and reruns with a negative control. Isolated local environments only; secrets masked in every artifact; anything unrun is reported not-proven, never passed.

plugins.name: release-gate
plugins.description: Runs three pre-launch passes (exposure, app-tests, perf) in sequence and returns one release posture — HOLD or ready — with three separate verdicts and one merged finding register. Deterministic arithmetic over union of findings; a lane that did not run holds the gate. Use when asked 'is this safe to ship', 'ready to deploy', or for go/no-go decisions before any production release.
